title: Newly provisioned administrators cannot use advertised password recovery
execution_level: Live Authentik + Console proxy + Identity DB; isolated regression
preconditions: Signed-in configured platform operator; active QA tenant created through New tenant; provider recovery configured.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Create a new tenant with a new administrator. 2. Read its administrator detail; recovery_deliveries contains link. 3. POST /v1/platform/access/tenants/{tenant}/administrators/{user}/password-recovery with delivery=link, reason and the current two revision timestamps; do not send an idempotency key.
expected_result: Issue an expiring provider recovery link for this active administrator, or accurately report unsupported capability before enabling Reset password.
actual_result: Live request returned 409 conflict: this sign-in provider does not support billing password recovery. Provisioning accepts/stores a 64-character hexadecimal provider uid as OIDC subject; recovery calls uuid.UUID on that subject. New regression reproduces 409 before the mocked provider recovery method is reached.
impact: The normal platform-created administrator cannot recover their password through the implemented feature. UI advertises an action that fails.
suggested_fix_or_next_check: Resolve the native provider account identifier through a trusted subject mapping; align eligibility and capability reporting with provisioning. Preserve account scope, email matching and restricted provider permissions.
retest_acceptance: A newly provisioned QA administrator receives a valid bounded link; native provider identifies the same account; wrong-account and ineligible-account cases remain refused.
fix_summary: Resolve opaque OIDC UID through a bounded email lookup, verify exact subject/email and reject ambiguous/incomplete responses. Preserve existing subjects and align advertised format eligibility.
retest_result: API/adapter regressions and native disposable-account recovery passed.

title: Recovery eligibility excludes the path used by platform provisioning
execution_level: Isolated adapter using production-shaped provider response + source verification
preconditions: Eligible external, active, verified, nonprivileged administrator; native UUID lookup succeeds; provider path bill/tenant-administrators.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Supply the recovery adapter a provider user with the fields required by provisioning and path=bill/tenant-administrators. 2. Call recover with a valid native UUID and matching email. 3. Observe rejection before the recovery POST.
expected_result: Platform-provisioned administrators within the intended application scope can recover through the same restricted boundary.
actual_result: AdministratorRecoveryProvider accepts only path=bill/pending-registration and raises AdministratorRecoveryUnavailableError for bill/tenant-administrators. AdministratorProvider.confirm_created requires bill/tenant-administrators. The new adapter test fails.
impact: Fixing only the subject parsing issue leaves a second recovery failure for platform-created accounts.
suggested_fix_or_next_check: Align the reviewed application account allowlist and native object-permission policy with both authorized enrollment paths; do not broadly enable unrelated provider users.
retest_acceptance: Both authorized registration and platform-provisioned accounts pass; unrelated paths, privileged accounts and mismatched emails remain rejected.
baseline_status: Confirmed in adapter regression; native path gated by PA-B001
fix_summary: Allow both supported account origins with provisioning marker checks. Add guarded native event handoff/backfill and object-only view/add/reset permissions required by the native POST gate; no global create/profile-change/delete authority.
retest_result: Native expression tests, native permission boundaries and newly provisioned account recovery passed.
remaining_checks: Native event worker must be running; recovery fails closed until its scoped permission handoff is processed.

title: ASCII DEL control character is persisted in tenant and administrator names
execution_level: Isolated real ASGI requests + SQLAlchemy fixture DB; provider adapter mocked
preconditions: Completed isolated installation and authorized platform operator.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. POST /v1/platform/tenants with name=Invalid\u007fName. 2. Repeat with administrator_name=Invalid\u007fName. 3. Create a valid tenant and PATCH its name to Invalid\u007fName.
expected_result: Reject control characters consistently with administrator access and other platform text validators; return 422 without saving the invalid value.
actual_result: Both create requests returned 201; editing returned 200. All three new negative tests fail. Validators reject codepoints below 32 but omit 127.
impact: Invisible control characters can contaminate displayed and exported names and make exact identification/search unreliable.
suggested_fix_or_next_check: Use a consistent approved text validator for tenant creation, administrator name and tenant edits.
retest_acceptance: All three cases return 422; ordinary Unicode names still succeed; no row containing DEL is committed.
fix_summary: Share control-character validation across tenant create/edit and administrator names; reject DEL and preserve Unicode.
retest_result: All three formerly failing API cases pass; Unicode-name regression passes.
remaining_checks: No automatic cleanup of previously stored names was performed.

preconditions: Existing workspace dependencies; run Auth server suite.

title: Native test modules are not safe to share one schema
preconditions: Fresh disposable schema; run platform setup native module followed by account review native module using the same IDENTITY_TEST_MYSQL_URL.
steps_to_reproduce: Run tests/test_platform_setup_mysql.py and tests/test_account_review_mysql.py in one pytest invocation pointing at the same disposable DB.
expected_result: Tests isolate or scope their records so committed setup events do not invalidate the next module.
actual_result: Setup passed; account-review rollback assertion failed at line 44 because it expected zero Outbox rows and found four setup events. Running each module in its own newly created schema passed both.
impact: Order-dependent false failure makes future combined native regression results unreliable.
suggested_fix_or_next_check: Use the added fresh-schema runner now; later correct fixture isolation or scope the assertions to the tested aggregate/tenant.
retest_acceptance: Tests pass alone and in either execution order without deleting unrelated rows.
baseline_status: Confirmed - isolated runner added; existing modules unchanged
fix_summary: Scope outbox assertions to the test tenant. Reusable runner verifies both modules alone and both shared-schema orders.
retest_result: Six native MySQL executions pass in fresh disposable schemas.
remaining_checks: These checks create model DDL; they are not migration round-trip evidence.

title: First OIDC discovery request exceeded the configured timeout
execution_level: Real browser + Authentik HTTPS tunnel + NextAuth
preconditions: Local services started; Authentik VM reached through configured SSH tunnel.
steps_to_reproduce: Open http://localhost:4310/login and click Continue to sign in immediately after startup.
expected_result: Reach the provider sign-in form, with a usable retry if discovery is temporarily slow.
actual_result: Initial attempt returned OAuthSignin and displayed the sign-in-service-unavailable message. Auth stderr recorded outgoing request timed out after 3500ms. Later fresh browser sessions authenticated and reached Console. Harness locator/transition failures in other attempts are not counted as application failures.
impact: A cold or slow provider can block a login attempt; permanent authentication failure is not established.
source_locations: mfes/apps/auth authentication configuration; local Authentik tunnel
suggested_fix_or_next_check: Measure discovery latency under cold start and confirm whether timeout/retry behavior needs adjustment; preserve safe error reporting.
retest_acceptance: Repeated cold and warm real logins succeed within the agreed limit or show a recoverable, correctly classified outage.
fix_summary: No speculative timeout/retry change. Preserve bounded provider behavior and investigate cold provider readiness separately.
retest_result: Fresh real logins succeeded; read-only native account lookups took 0.866, 0.375 and 0.388 seconds. This is not a cold OIDC benchmark.
remaining_checks: Cold OIDC discovery and production latency remain unproven. Intermediate session-loading failure retained in the live ledger; final settled-page rerun passed.
